messages:
alexr: Heads up — after enabling INT8 kernels on the longctx perf branch I'm seeing steady mem growth on kv-cache over ~1M tokens. Looks like fragmentation + paging churn. Repro script attached in thread.

maria_l: Can you paste the heap/profile snapshot? Is this with the new compact-on-evict heuristic?

alexr: Snapshot (trimmed):
```
KV entries: 3.2M
Allocated pages: 3824 (4k pages)
Free segments: 512 (avg hole 1.2 pages)
Pinned pages: 128
INT8 cache size: 1.02 GiB
FP16 cache size: 2.14 GiB
RSS delta over run: +420 MiB
CPU: kernel INT8_mm_accel selected for 80% of steps
```
Seems like INT8 reduces per-entry size but increases # allocations and leaves small holes that we don't compact. Paging reads spike when KF lookup falls back.

ben_c: Interesting — could be our slab allocator fragmentation because quantized blobs are not power-of-two aligned after packing. INT8 packs more tightly -> more leftover slack. Did you try running the compactor?

alexr: Yes, I ran the in-proc compactor (force-compact) midway: RSS drops ~160MiB immediately but growth resumes. Compactor appears to free segments but not reclaim the small scattered holes.

sophie: Do we have telemetry for eviction latency / page reuse ratio? Might indicate whether reuse is suffering.

perf-bot: perf snapshot: https://perf.redwood/internal/8231 (flamegraph + pagewalk heatmap). Key points: KV page fault rate up 3.6x vs FP16 baseline; batch size distribution unaffected; kernel selection time increased 5ms on avg for mixed-precision switch.

maria_l: Also saw slight quality delta on eval set when forcing INT8-only: avg perplexity +1.2 and some top-1 token mismatches for long contexts (>=8k). Could be quantization + cache truncation precision interplay.

ben_c: Hypothesis: when KV entries are quantized to INT8 we store metadata differently (packed per-block). On eviction we writeback compressed pages; on reload we dequantize into transient buffers. If the dequantize path chooses fused kernels (fast path) vs fallback path we may get subtle numerical divergences — plus the eviction/restore reorders memory layout causing cache misses.

alexr: Repro steps I used:
```
# run long generation with longctx dataset
python tools/repro_longctx.py --model rdx-3b --quant int8 --ctx 16384 --tokens 1_000_000 --kv-mode paged
# watch mem
watch -n 5 "pmap $(pidof runtime) | grep total"
```
Observed steady per-token mem growth around 0.4 KiB/token after 200k tokens.

maria_l: Can you attach the per-token latency distribution? If paging is happening, P99 should jump when eviction triggers.

alexr: P99 shows spikes aligned with compaction windows. Average latency stable, but 99.9th spikes +120ms during page fetches. Batching heuristics unchanged; batch sizes not increasing.

ben_c: Two-pronged plan: (1) add a small-page coalescer that merges adjacent holes every N evictions, (2) change quant packing to keep minimal alignment to reduce leftover slack. Also add a metric: "kv.hole_bytes" and "kv.coalesce_runs".

sophie: +1. Also propose we add a verification pass that compares dequantized cached KV against a reference FP16 slice for a small sample to detect bit-level divergence early. Run that during canary.

alexr: Started a branch with coalescer + metrics. Early run: hole_bytes down 28% and RSS growth rate reduced to 0.15 KiB/token. But the small eval perplexity delta remains (~+0.9).

maria_l: For the quality drop we should check: (A) dequantization numerical bias (B) overflow/underflow in mixed-kernel matmuls when using packed INT8 + BF16 activations (C) KV truncation near eviction boundaries.

ben_c: I profiled matrix mul kernel variants: INT8_mm_accel gives slightly different rounding than ref INT8_mm_precise. Swap to precise on restore path -> perf cost +3% but perplexity delta disappears in sample. Might be acceptable for Dedicated/Private tiers.

alexr: Good find. Could make kernel policy per-traffic-class: fast kernel for low-latency, precise kernel when cache restore happens or during canary eval. Need runtime flag.

sophie: Ops implications: switching kernels increases GPU util; we should surface per-kernel cost in Console. Also document that INT8 may need periodic compaction for long-lived streams.

maria_l: Action items assigned:
- ben_c: land coalescer + alignment change + metrics (PR: #4123)
- alexr: add kernel-policy hook + repro harness for dequant compare (PR: #4124)
- sophie: add alert for kv.hole_bytes growth > 200MiB and p99 latency delta > 80ms (SLO review)

ben_c: I'll also add workload that simulates many small prefix updates to reproduce fragmentation faster and include it in nightly perf.

alexr: Thanks — will soak the patch on staging. If anyone wants the raw traces I pushed pprof + pmap outputs to the perf link. :thumbsup:

maria_l: Nice. Keep notes on which customer tiers get the precise restore by default. We may gate by Dedicated/private.

sophie: +1. Also add a KB note for Solutions about expected mem behavior with INT8 on very long contexts.

perf-bot: auto-note: issue tracked as KVCACHE-349, nightly job added kvcache-frag-repro.

alexr: Closing for now — will reopen if repro changes.
